title: Compound past and participles
objectives: I can use the Portuguese present perfect (ter + participle) to talk about actions repeated or continuing up to now.
I can form regular and irregular past participles and choose between long and short forms.
I can use participles as adjectives and make them agree with the noun.
I can say that something has just happened with acabar de, and use já, ainda não, nunca and ultimamente naturally.

example.pt: Terminar a faculdade foi a maior conquista da minha vida.
example.en: Finishing college was the greatest achievement of my life.

example.pt: Trabalhar fora do país tem sido uma experiência incrível.
example.en: Working abroad has been an incredible experience.

vocabulary.note: Realizar um sonho means to make a dream come true. It does not mean to realize in the sense of becoming aware (that is perceber or se dar conta).

example.pt: Ela realizou o sonho de abrir o próprio restaurante.
example.en: She fulfilled her dream of opening her own restaurant.

vocabulary.en: to manage to, to succeed in

example.pt: Finalmente consegui marcar a consulta.
example.en: I finally managed to book the appointment.

vocabulary.note: Also means a sale or special offer in a shop.

example.pt: Ela tem trabalhado muito e merece essa promoção.
example.en: She has been working hard and deserves this promotion.

example.pt: A formatura da minha irmã foi no sábado.
example.en: My sister's graduation was on Saturday.

vocabulary.note: Unlike English news, notícia is countable: uma notícia, duas notícias.

example.pt: Acabei de ler uma notícia estranha.
example.en: I just read a strange piece of news.

example.pt: Recentemente, a cidade tem recebido muitos turistas.
example.en: Recently, the city has been receiving many tourists.

example.pt: Ultimamente tenho dormido pouco.
example.en: Lately I have been sleeping little.

example.pt: Nos últimos tempos, os preços têm subido muito.
example.en: In recent times, prices have been rising a lot.

example.pt: A mudança de cidade tem sido difícil para todos.
example.en: The move to another city has been hard for everyone.

vocabulary.note: To move house is mudar de casa or mudar para a cidade X; the reflexive se mudar is also very common.

example.pt: Meu irmão tem mudado muito ultimamente.
example.en: My brother has been changing a lot lately.

example.pt: Tenho criado o hábito de acordar cedo.
example.en: I have been building the habit of waking up early.

example.pt: Ainda não me acostumei com o frio daqui.
example.en: I still haven't gotten used to the cold here.

example.pt: Meu inglês tem melhorado bastante.
example.en: My English has been improving a lot.

example.pt: O trânsito tem piorado a cada ano.
example.en: The traffic has been getting worse every year.

vocabulary.note: Masculine, even though it ends in -a. Likewise o tema, o sistema, o programa.

example.pt: O problema é que o aplicativo não abre.
example.en: The problem is that the app won't open.

example.pt: Ainda não encontramos uma solução.
example.en: We still haven't found a solution.

example.pt: O técnico já resolveu o problema.
example.en: The technician has already solved the problem.

example.pt: O esforço dela tem dado resultado.
example.en: Her effort has been paying off.

vocabulary.note: Followed by de: desistir de um plano.

example.pt: Nunca desisti do meu sonho de viajar pelo mundo.
example.en: I never gave up on my dream of traveling the world.

example.pt: Já adiei a reunião duas vezes.
example.en: I have already postponed the meeting twice.

example.pt: Ele superou o medo de falar em público.
example.en: He overcame his fear of public speaking.

example.pt: Tenho tido algumas dificuldades com a nova língua.
example.en: I have been having some difficulties with the new language.

vocabulary.note: Followed by an infinitive. In Brazil, acabar is normally in the preterite: acabei de chegar.

example.pt: Acabei de chegar em casa.
example.en: I have just gotten home.

example.pt: Ainda não li o e-mail.
example.en: I haven't read the e-mail yet.

dialogues.title: Colocando a conversa em dia
dialogues.context: Ana and Carlos run into each other at a café after several months without seeing each other.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Carlos! Quanto tempo! Como você tem passado?
lines.en: Carlos! It's been ages! How have you been?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Oi, Ana! Tenho trabalhado muito, mas tá tudo bem. E você?
lines.en: Hi, Ana! I've been working a lot, but everything is fine. And you?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Eu também. Ultimamente tenho corrido todas as manhãs, e isso tem melhorado meu humor.
lines.en: Me too. Lately I've been running every morning, and that has been improving my mood.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Que bom! Eu nunca consegui criar esse hábito. Já tentei várias vezes e sempre desisti.
lines.en: Great! I've never managed to build that habit. I've tried several times and always given up.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Comecei devagar. No início, só caminhava. Agora já corro cinco quilômetros.
lines.en: I started slowly. At first I only walked. Now I already run five kilometers.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Puxa, que conquista! Você viu que a Marina se formou?
lines.en: Wow, what an achievement! Did you see that Marina graduated?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Vi, sim! Acabei de ver as fotos da formatura no celular. Ela estava tão feliz.
lines.en: I did! I just looked at the graduation photos on my phone. She looked so happy.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Ela tem estudado muito nos últimos anos. Merecia essa alegria.
lines.en: She has been studying a lot in recent years. She deserved this joy.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Verdade. E a sua mudança pra São Paulo? Você já se acostumou?
lines.en: True. And your move to São Paulo? Have you gotten used to it yet?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Ainda não totalmente. O trânsito tem piorado a cada mês, mas eu gosto da cidade.
lines.en: Not completely yet. The traffic has been getting worse every month, but I like the city.

dialogues.title: Um problema no escritório
dialogues.context: The office printer keeps breaking down. Beatriz, Rafael and Helena try to find a solution before a deadline.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Rafael, a impressora tem dado problema de novo. Você sabe o que está acontecendo?
lines.en: Rafael, the printer has been giving trouble again. Do you know what's going on?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Tem dado problema desde segunda. Já abri um chamado com o suporte.
lines.en: It has been giving trouble since Monday. I've already opened a ticket with support.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: E eles já responderam?
lines.en: And have they answered yet?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Ainda não. Acabaram de me mandar uma mensagem dizendo que vão analisar.
lines.en: Not yet. They just sent me a message saying they will look into it.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Gente, enquanto isso eu tenho usado a impressora do andar de cima. Não é a solução perfeita, mas resolve.
lines.en: Guys, in the meantime I've been using the printer upstairs. It's not the perfect solution, but it works.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Preciso imprimir o contrato hoje, e o cliente já adiou a entrega duas vezes.
lines.en: Good idea. I need to print the contract today, and the client has already postponed the delivery twice.

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Então vai lá em cima agora. Eu continuo esperando o suporte.
lines.en: Then go upstairs now. I'll keep waiting for support.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Você já tentou desligar e ligar de novo? Às vezes funciona.
lines.en: Have you tried turning it off and on again? Sometimes it works.

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Já tentei três vezes. Nada.
lines.en: I've tried three times. Nothing.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Tudo bem, eu vou lá em cima. Obrigada, Helena!
lines.en: Okay, I'll go upstairs. Thanks, Helena!

dialogues.title: Notícias da semana
dialogues.context: Luísa and Pedro talk about a piece of local news and how they get around the city.

lines.speaker: Luísa
lines.pt: Pedro, você viu a notícia? A nossa cidade acabou de ganhar um prêmio de melhor transporte público.
lines.en: Pedro, did you see the news? Our city has just won a best public transport award.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Sério? Nos últimos tempos o ônibus tem chegado no horário, então faz sentido.
lines.en: Really? Lately the bus has been arriving on time, so it makes sense.

lines.speaker: Luísa
lines.pt: Pois é. A prefeitura tem investido em corredores exclusivos para ônibus, e isso tem feito diferença.
lines.en: Exactly. The city government has been investing in bus-only lanes, and that has made a difference.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Eu mesmo tenho deixado o carro em casa quase todos os dias.
lines.en: I myself have been leaving the car at home almost every day.

lines.speaker: Luísa
lines.pt: Sério? Eu nunca tive coragem de deixar o carro. Tenho medo de perder tempo esperando.
lines.en: Really? I've never had the courage to leave the car. I'm afraid of wasting time waiting.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Eu tinha o mesmo medo, mas agora chego mais cedo do que antes.
lines.en: I had the same fear, but now I arrive earlier than before.

lines.speaker: Luísa
lines.pt: Então vou tentar na segunda. Você já viu os horários novos?
lines.en: Then I'll try on Monday. Have you seen the new timetables yet?

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Já vi, sim. Vou te mandar o link agora.
lines.en: I have. I'll send you the link now.

grammar.title: Ter + participle: repeated or continuing action up to now
grammar.explanation:
The pretérito perfeito composto is formed with the present tense of ter plus the past participle: tenho estudado, tem feito, temos visto. The participle never changes for gender or number here; only ter changes. Watch the third person: singular tem, plural têm (same sound, different spelling).

The tense looks like the English present perfect, but it is used much more narrowly. It describes an action that has been repeated or has continued from the past up to the present: Tenho estudado muito means 'I have been studying a lot (lately)'. It cannot report a single finished event or a life experience. For those, Portuguese uses the simple preterite: Já estudei isso na escola (I have studied this at school), Nunca fui ao Nordeste (I have never been to the Northeast), Já comi (I have eaten).

A quick test: if 'lately', 'repeatedly' or 'these days' fits the English sentence, use ter + participle. In everyday Brazilian speech this tense is less common than in writing. Speakers often prefer estou fazendo, ando fazendo or venho fazendo for the same idea, but ter + participle is fully natural, especially with ultimamente, nos últimos tempos and desde.

examples.pt: Tenho estudado português todos os dias.
examples.en: I have been studying Portuguese every day.

examples.pt: Ela tem chegado tarde ultimamente.
examples.en: She has been arriving late lately.

examples.pt: Os preços têm subido muito.
examples.en: Prices have been rising a lot.

examples.pt: Nós temos conversado bastante sobre isso.
examples.en: We have been talking about this quite a lot.

examples.pt: Já estudei isso na escola.
examples.en: I have studied this at school.

examples.pt: Nunca fui ao Nordeste.
examples.en: I have never been to the Northeast.

grammar.title: Regular and irregular participles
grammar.explanation:
Regular participles are easy: verbs in -ar take -ado (falar, falado) and verbs in -er and -ir take -ido (comer, comido; partir, partido). Only a small group is irregular, and they are all very frequent, so learn them as vocabulary. Verbs built on these also share the irregularity: desfazer, desfeito; prever, previsto; descobrir, descoberto; reescrever, reescrito.

A second group has two participles. The long regular form (ganhado, gastado, pagado, aceitado, entregado, acendido) is traditionally used with ter, and the short form (ganho, gasto, pago, aceito, entregue, aceso) with ser and estar. In speech in Brazil the short forms of ganhar, gastar and pagar are also heard with ter (tenho pago, tinha ganho). If you use the long form with ter, you are always correct.

Ser and ir have the participles sido and ido: Tem sido difícil (It has been hard), Ela tem ido à academia (She has been going to the gym).

examples.pt: Tenho feito exercícios todos os dias.
examples.en: I have been exercising every day.

examples.pt: Ela tem dito a mesma coisa há semanas.
examples.en: She has been saying the same thing for weeks.

examples.pt: Eles têm visto muitos filmes brasileiros.
examples.en: They have been watching a lot of Brazilian films.

examples.pt: Ele tem escrito artigos para o jornal.
examples.en: He has been writing articles for the newspaper.

examples.pt: Tenho vindo aqui toda semana.
examples.en: I have been coming here every week.

examples.pt: Tem sido um ano muito difícil.
examples.en: It has been a very hard year.

grammar.title: Participles as adjectives: agreement
grammar.explanation:
Participles are also adjectives. After estar (a resulting state) or ser (a passive action) they agree with the noun in gender and number, like any adjective: a porta está aberta, os documentos estão escritos, as lojas foram fechadas. This is the opposite of the ter construction, where the participle stays fixed: Ela tem aberto a porta (she has been opening the door) versus A porta está aberta (the door is open).

Agreement also shows who is speaking: a man says Estou cansado, a woman says Estou cansada, and a mixed group says Estamos cansados. Many common adjectives are participles in disguise: cansado, preocupado, perdido, decidido, casado, cheio, aberto, fechado.

Participles also appear alone as short reactions and summaries: Feito! (Done!), Combinado! (Agreed!), Resolvido! (Sorted!), Dito isso... (That said...). Note that these are invariable only because they stand for a whole situation.

examples.pt: A loja está aberta até as dez.
examples.en: The shop is open until ten.

examples.pt: Os documentos estão escritos em inglês.
examples.en: The documents are written in English.

examples.pt: Estamos cansadas depois da viagem.
examples.en: We are tired after the trip.

examples.pt: A conta já está paga.
examples.en: The bill is already paid.

examples.pt: A reunião foi adiada para sexta.
examples.en: The meeting was postponed to Friday.

examples.pt: Problema resolvido!
examples.en: Problem solved!

grammar.title: Acabar de, já, ainda não, nunca
grammar.explanation:
To say something has just happened, use acabar de plus an infinitive. In Brazilian Portuguese acabar is almost always in the preterite: Acabei de chegar (I have just arrived), Ela acabou de sair (She has just left). The present form acabo de chegar sounds formal or European.

For completed events and experiences, the simple preterite is the normal partner of já (already), ainda não (not yet) and nunca (never): Já comi, Ainda não li o e-mail, Nunca vi esse filme. Do not use ter + participle here; Já tenho comido would mean 'I keep eating' and Nunca tenho visto would be read as a present habit.

Use ter + participle with ultimamente, nos últimos tempos, recentemente and desde when the action is repeated or ongoing. Negative sentences work the same way: Ultimamente não tenho dormido bem. Also note that já can mean 'right away' (Já vou! I'm coming!) and ainda can mean 'still' (Ainda moro aqui).

rows: Lately I have been eating badly.
I have been going to the gym.

examples.pt: Ela acabou de sair do trabalho.
examples.en: She has just left work.

examples.pt: Eles acabaram de chegar da viagem.
examples.en: They have just come back from the trip.

examples.pt: Já resolvi o problema.
examples.en: I have already solved the problem.

examples.pt: Ainda não li a mensagem.
examples.en: I haven't read the message yet.

examples.pt: Nunca desisti dos meus planos.
examples.en: I have never given up on my plans.

examples.pt: Ultimamente não tenho dormido bem.
examples.en: Lately I haven't been sleeping well.

culture.title: Formaturas, vestibular and talking about progress
culture.text:
Achievements are celebrated loudly in Brazil. A formatura is a major family event, with a ceremony, a party and often a formal ball, and many graduating classes hire a company to organize it for months in advance. Getting into a public university through the vestibular or the Enem exam is also announced to friends and relatives, who shower the new student with congratulations: Parabéns pela conquista! People even tell the story of the aprovado, the student who was approved, with the same pride as a wedding.

In everyday talk, Brazilians often ask how things have been going with phrases like Como você tem andado? or Tem feito o quê da vida? The expected answer is a short progress report with the compound past: Tenho trabalhado bastante, Tenho corrido de manhã. Because the tense describes an ongoing stretch of time, it sounds friendly and interested rather than final. For single past events, people simply switch back to the preterite: Comecei um curso novo, Mudei de emprego.

It is also common to encourage someone with Não desista! and to describe difficulties with the word perrengue (a small mess or mishap): Tenho passado por cada perrengue! Being open about both problems and solutions is a normal part of catching up with friends.

paragraphs.pt: Faz um ano que me mudei de Curitiba para Recife, e muita coisa tem mudado desde então.
paragraphs.en: It has been a year since I moved from Curitiba to Recife, and a lot has changed since then.

paragraphs.pt: No começo, eu tinha dificuldade para me acostumar com o calor e com o sotaque das pessoas. Ultimamente, porém, tenho me sentido em casa.
paragraphs.en: At first I had difficulty getting used to the heat and to people's accent. Lately, however, I have been feeling at home.

paragraphs.pt: No trabalho, tenho aprendido muito. Minha chefe tem confiado em mim e, no mês passado, recebi minha primeira promoção.
paragraphs.en: At work I have been learning a lot. My boss has been trusting me and, last month, I received my first promotion.

paragraphs.pt: Também tenho criado novos hábitos: acordo cedo e tenho caminhado na praia quase todos os dias. Antes eu sempre adiava esse tipo de coisa.
paragraphs.en: I have also been building new habits: I wake up early and have been walking on the beach almost every day. Before, I always put that kind of thing off.

paragraphs.pt: Nem tudo foi fácil. Por causa do aluguel caro, tenho gastado mais do que eu gostaria, e ainda não encontrei um apartamento perfeito.
paragraphs.en: Not everything was easy. Because of the expensive rent, I have been spending more than I would like, and I still haven't found a perfect apartment.

paragraphs.pt: Mesmo assim, acabei de assinar um contrato novo, em um bairro mais tranquilo. Agora que esse problema está resolvido, posso pensar nos próximos sonhos.
paragraphs.en: Even so, I have just signed a new lease, in a quieter neighborhood. Now that this problem is solved, I can think about my next dreams.
